name: Sable Noir Yuzu-Black Pepper Tablets
description: Thin, hand-pressed cocoa-analog tablets with a yuzu oil center and cracked black pepper suspended in the shell — part of Sable Noir's premium 'Contrast' line aimed at Tier 3-4 palates.
flavor_profile: Bright citrus from yuzu, a dark bittersweet cocoa-analog base, and a slow prickle of black pepper that builds on the finish; melt-forward texture
cultural_context: Sable Noir positions itself as the thinking person's confection brand; their products are often found at gallery openings, corporate lounges, and Tier 4 dinner parties where the act of offering candy is itself a small performance of taste.
story_hooks: Sable Noir is quietly using a black-market yuzu extract supplier whose agricultural operation exists outside city licensing — exposing it would collapse the brand's premium image.
A character receives a Sable Noir box with a message pressed into the tablet surface using a micro-engraving technique — someone is using confection as a covert communication medium.
The 'Contrast' line is accused of plagiarizing a Tier 1 street candy maker's flavor combination, sparking an IP dispute that crosses every tier.
